name: Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility (KA171) - student mobility for studies
provider: European Commission / national agencies, implemented by individual European HEIs
whoCanApply: Students already ENROLLED at a Tunisian higher education institution that holds a signed KA171 inter-institutional agreement with a specific European HEI. Tunisia is an eligible Partner Country (Region 3, Southern Neighbourhood). Not open to individual applicants - you cannot apply as a private person and you cannot use it to enrol in a European degree.
subjectScope: Open: handbook states 'Student and staff mobility can take place in any subject area or academic discipline.' Music production would qualify if the agreement covers it.
coverage: Individual support paid at the rate of the DESTINATION country: EUR 900/month for Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden; EUR 850/month for Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Latvia, Malta, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain; EUR 800/month for Bulgaria, Croatia, North Macedonia, Hungary, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Turkiye. Travel support by distance band: EUR 309 (500-1999 km, non-green) or EUR 417 green; EUR 395 (2000-2999 km) or EUR 535 green. Organisational support of EUR 500 per participant covers visa/insurance/linguistic preparation but is paid to the institutions, not the student.
duration: Physical mobility period can last from 60 days to 12 months (5-30 days for short-term doctoral or blended). MAXIMUM 12 MONTHS - structurally cannot cover a full 2-year master's.
numberOfAwards: Set per bilateral project; typically 2-10 students per agreement per year
deadline: Institution-level internal calls, usually Feb-April for the following academic year. The KA171 call for institutions closes annually in February.
howToApply: Through the international relations office of the Tunisian home university, not directly to the European host or to the Commission.
requiresAdmissionFirst: No - but requires current enrolment at a Tunisian HEI with an existing agreement, which is a harder bar for this candidate
competitiveness: Moderate within a given agreement, but access is gated by whether his Tunisian home institution has an agreement at all
notes: VERDICT ON THE QUESTION ASKED: Erasmus+ ICM CANNOT fund a full master's degree for a Tunisian. The handbook caps the physical mobility period at 12 months and the scheme is defined as credit mobility - a limited period of study abroad within ongoing studies at the home institution, after which the student returns home and the credits are recognised there. It therefore DOES NOT BELONG in this funding file as a route to a September 2027 master's. The full-degree Erasmus+ instrument for a Tunisian is Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (already settled: DIGICREA, ReSound, WAVES). Additionally, this candidate is graduating now, so by Sept 2027 he would no longer be enrolled at a Tunisian HEI and would be ineligible even for the exchange version.

name: Offre nationale des bourses pour des etudes de mastere et de doctorat a l'etranger (bourses d'etudes a l'etranger)
provider: Ministere de l'Enseignement Superieur et de la Recherche Scientifique, Tunisia - DGAEMUET, portal best.rnu.tn

WHETHER A MUSIC PRODUCTION / STUDIO CRAFT MASTER'S IS AN ACCEPTED FIELD MUST BE CONFIRMED FROM THE CIRCULAIRE 2027-2028 PDF. This is the single most consequential unknown in the whole file.
coverage: THE MOST COMPLETE PACKAGE FOUND FOR A TUNISIAN. For EU destinations: EUR 800 per month, structured as EUR 600 grant plus EUR 200 as a loan repayable over 10 years. For Canada: CAD 1,000 per month (CAD 800 grant + CAD 200 repayable loan over 10 years). PLUS tuition fees, social security, compulsory health insurance, study permits and transport costs.

numberOfAwards: UNVERIFIED - the portal reports 3,638 scholarship/loan applications in 2025 and 1,870 partner universities abroad, but does not publish an award count

EXPECTED 2027-2028 WINDOW: circulaire published around October 2026, applications closing approximately November-December 2026, results around January 2027. The 2026-2027 circulaire was posted on 24 October 2025. EXACT DEADLINE UNVERIFIED - the circulaire is a downloadable PDF that could not be retrieved.
opens: Approximately October, with the annual 'Circulaire' and country annexes

IF SO, THIS DRIVES HIS ENTIRE TIMELINE: he would need European admission decisions in hand by roughly Nove…
requiresWorkExperience: No - it is explicitly aimed at recent laureates, which suits a candidate graduating now

Two things must be checked IMMEDIATELY, not in 2027: (1) whether arts/music/AFAM-type programmes are within the eligible fields, and (2) whether a prior admission letter is required at application, because that would pull his whole application calendar forward by six to nine months. The 2026-2027 circulaire page: https://best.rnu.tn/offre-nationale-des-bourses-pour-des-etudes-de-mastere-et-de-doctorat-a-letranger-au-titre-de-lannee-universitaire-2026-2027/ . name: France Excellence Eiffel scholarship (master's level) - SUBJECT-SCOPE NEGATIVE
provider: Ministere de l'Europe et des Affaires etrangeres, administered by Campus France; relayed in Tunisia by the Institut francais de Tunisie
whoCanApply: International students nominated by a French higher education institution. ageLimit: Up to 29 years old at master's level. He would be 24-26 at entry, so he is comfortably inside.
subjectScope: NO - THIS IS THE DISQUALIFIER. The eligible fields at master's level are: biology and health; ecological transition; mathematics and digital; science and engineering; French history, language and civilisation; law and political science; economics and management. ARTS, MUSIC AND CREATIVE PRACTICE ARE NOT AMONG THE ELIGIBLE FIELDS. A music production or studio craft master's does not fall into any Eiffel discipline. (An audio-signal-processing or music-informatics master's inside an engineering school could arguably fall under 'mathematics and digital' or 'science and engineering' - that is the only way Eiffel becomes live for him, and it would mean choosing an engineering-framed programme rather than a conservatoire one.)
coverage: EUR 1,181 per month at master's level, plus an international return air ticket and social security cover. Does not pay tuition, but French public tuition is low.
duration: Up to 12 months for master's (up to 24 in some configurations - UNVERIFIED)
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 8 January 2026 for receipt of applications by Campus France (2026 session). EXPECTED 2027 CYCLE: approximately 8 January 2027 - and note the FRENCH INSTITUTION must assemble and submit the file well before that, so his contact with the institution has to start in autumn 2026.
opens: Autumn (institutions build files from roughly October)
howToApply: The French institution submits on his behalf to candidatures.eiffel@campusfrance.org - he must first secure the institution's willingness to nominate him
requiresAdmissionFirst: Effectively YES - the institution nominating him must have him as an applicant/admittee
languageRequirement: French for French-taught programmes - he is fluent, which is a genuine advantage here
notes: IMPORTANT STRATEGIC POINT. Eiffel is the largest French award a Tunisian can access and his French fluency and age both fit, but the discipline list excludes the arts. This is the SECOND scheme in his file (after DAAD's music award) where the subject rather than the nationality is the barrier - the pattern is that generalist excellence schemes fund STEM and social science, while arts funding sits in a separate, much smaller ecosystem. If he wanted Eiffel he would have to reframe his target towards an engineering-school audio/signal-processing master's (e.g. at Universite Gustave Eiffel or an ESAV/UBO-adjacent technical route). Also relevant from the same source: the Institut francais de Tunisie / French Embassy run a Master 2 Recherche excellence scholarship, created in 2013, financing M2 research mobility WITHIN a Franco-Tunisian inter-university partnership or double-degree agreement, with calls launched annually in MAY - that requires an existing partnership between his Tunisian institution and a French one, and is research-M2-shaped rather than professional-master-shaped. UNVERIFIED for arts eligibility.

name: Borse di studio del Governo italiano a studenti stranieri - Corsi AFAM (2 ciclo) and Laurea magistrale
provider: Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI), via the Study in Italy portal
whoCanApply: Foreign citizens of beneficiary countries. The bando states selection 'viene effettuata sulla base del criterio della cittadinanza' - selection is on the basis of citizenship, and a candidate may compete for one country only. Additional bars quoted from art. 2.4.1: must NOT be enrolled in or hold a qualification from an Italian secondary school; must NOT be enrolled in or hold a qualification from an Italian higher education institution (university or AFAM) on Italian territory; must NOT enrol in any year other than the first.
ageLimit: YES AND IT MATTERS: for Laurea magistrale (art. 1.1) and AFAM 1st and 2nd cycle (art. 1.2), applicants must be 'di eta non superiore a 28 anni alla data di scadenza del presente bando' - not older than 28 at the closing date (for the 2026-27 bando: born on or after 27 March 1997). At 24-26 he is inside, but this is a real cliff-edge if he defers beyond 2027.
subjectScope: YES - EXPLICITLY. Art. 1.2 covers 'Corsi di Alta formazione artistica, musicale e coreutica (AFAM)' at both 1st and 2nd cycle. This is one of the very few state scholarship schemes anywhere in Europe that names music conservatoire study as an eligible category. It pairs directly with the Italian conservatoires and Saint Louis College of Music Rome already on his target list.
coverage: EUR 10,800 total for the 9-month award, paid into an Italian bank account in three instalments: EUR 5,500 first, EUR 2,300 from February, EUR 3,000 from June. PLUS a collective medical insurance policy paid for by MAECI covering illness and accident for the duration of the scholarship (pre-existing conditions and dental care excluded). TUITION IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY COVERED: the bando says some institutions grant exemption from tuition and university contributions under the university-autonomy rules (D.Lgs. 68/2012), that beneficiaries must check with their chosen institution, that any fees due are NOT reimbursable by MAECI, and that regional taxes are always payable by the student and not reimbursable.
duration: 9 months with a FIXED start: 1 November 2026 to 31 July 2027 for the 2026-27 bando, which 'non puo essere differita all'anno accademico successivo'. Renewable for a subsequent year of a multi-year course (renewal is prioritised for those evidencing at least 15 CFU).
numberOfAwards: Allocated per country; the number for Tunisia is not published in the bando. Note art. 5 reserves 3 'Attanasio' scholarships for candidates from Morocco, Nigeria and DR Congo in international-relations fields - not applicable to him.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 14:00 Italian time, 26 March 2026 (with a follow-up documentation deadline of 14:00 on 1 July 2026). EXPECTED 2027-2028 WINDOW: bando published around late February/early March 2027, closing around 26 March 2027. Safely after September 2026.
howToApply: Exclusively online, after registration, through the Study in Italy portal at https://studyinitaly.esteri.it
requiresAdmissionFirst: NOT AT APPLICATION - but a regular enrolment certificate at the Italian institution is 'condizione indispensabile per l'erogazione della borsa'. The bando warns that for some AFAM courses enrolment is conditional on passing an entrance exam (prova di ammissione) and/or a pre-enrolment procedure, so…
languageRequirement: B2. For Italian-taught courses: a certificate attesting Italian at CEFR B2 (or a certificate from the director of Italian-language university courses attended). For English-taught courses: a certificate attesting English at CEFR B2 - and 'per l'iscrizione a corsi che si svolgono interamente in lingua inglese non e richiesta la conoscenza della lingua italiana'. HE HAS NEITHER YET - an English B2 …
notes: MAJOR EXCLUSION TO NOTE - it removes several obvious Italian options: MAECI scholarships are explicitly NOT awarded for 'corsi di Laurea triennale (1 ciclo), eccetto che per i corsi AFAM', for single-cycle degrees, and critically NOT for 'master universitari di I e II livello, corsi di specializzazione, corsi universitari della durata di un anno' - so ONE-YEAR ITALIAN MASTERS AND 'MASTER UNIVERSITARIO' PROGRAMMES ARE INELIGIBLE. Only a two-year Laurea magistrale or a two-year AFAM Diploma accademico di secondo livello qualifies. This directly shapes which Italian programme he should target: a conservatoire biennio in music/electronic music/sound technology, NOT a one-year professional master. Also excluded: employees of the Italian public administration and their first-degree descendants; anyone who has held a MAECI research scholarship in the last 5 academic years. The award is compatible with Erasmus and Erasmus+. This scheme STACKS with the Italian regional DSU grant (EUR 7,072-7,171/yr fuori sede, AFAM-eligible, ISEE parificato) already established in his file - together they would be a workable Italian package.

name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Scholarships for non-EU citizens (Romanian Government Scholarships)
provider: Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE) with the Ministry of Education and Research (MER)

coverage: Tuition-free study, a monthly stipend and accommodation support are the standard components. EXACT AMOUNTS UNVERIFIED - the studyinromania.gov.ro scholarship pages could not be read directly.

The combination of no nationality list, no field restriction beyond medicine, no admission-first requirement and a French-language application platform makes this the most accessible of the Central/Eastern European state schemes for him. THE WEAKNESS IS THE DESTINATION, NOT THE FUNDING: Romania is not a strong market for studio craft, mixing and mastering education, so the real question is whether any Romanian institution runs a programme worth doing. That is a programme question, not a funding question, and sits outside this file.

The official field wording could not be read from the NAWA site itself (the 'Information for applicants' and 'Call for proposals' pages returned navigation only) - the field list is drawn from NAWA-derived summaries including SGGW Warsaw's institutional page and study.gov.pl, so treat the exact wording as UNVERIFIED while treating the STEM restriction as reliably established.

name: Estonian Government Scholarships under bilateral agreements
provider: Estonian Ministry of Education and Research / Harno (Education and Youth Board)
whoCanApply: Foreign nationals of countries with which Estonia has a bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreement. TUNISIA IS EXPLICITLY ON THAT LIST, alongside Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czechia, Cyprus, Egypt, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Mexico, Moldova, China, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, South Korea, Slovenia, Spain, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Turkiye, Ukraine and the USA.
subjectScope: YES - master's and doctoral programmes 'in all fields' are supported (only BACHELOR'S study is restricted, to fields related to Estonian language and culture). A music production or sound master's at EAMT Tallinn is therefore within scope.
coverage: EUR 350 per month for bachelor's and master's students (EUR 660 for doctoral). Harno states explicitly that 'other costs are not covered' - SO THERE IS NO TUITION WAIVER, NO TRAVEL AND NO INSURANCE. At EAMT, international tuition runs from EUR 1,750 to EUR 14,000 per year depending on programme and country of origin, so this is a living-cost top-up only and must be stacked with an institutional tuition waiver.
duration: Degree study is supported; exchange study is capped at a minimum of one month and a maximum of 10 calendar months per year
numberOfAwards: Not published as a number, but Harno states 'only about 10% of applicants receive the scholarship each year'
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: 2 September to 1 October, 23:59 Estonian time, for the 2025/26 academic year. EXPECTED 2027 CYCLE: 2 September - 1 October 2027 for a September 2027 start, i.e. applied for AFTER arrival/admission rather than before. UNVERIFIED whether the window instead runs a year ahead - CHECK THIS, because if the window is Sept-Oct 2026 for 2027 entry, it becomes a deadline he could easily miss.
howToApply: Online via Harno. CRITICAL: 'Applications must include a confirmation letter from an Estonian higher education institution documenting admission before the deadline; submissions lacking this will not be processed.'
requiresAdmissionFirst: YES - ABSOLUTELY. An admission confirmation letter from the Estonian institution must be inside the application or it is not processed at all.
languageRequirement: Set by the institution; EAMT teaches its international programmes in English
competitiveness: Very high - roughly a 10% success rate
notes: PAIR THIS WITH THE EAMT INSTITUTIONAL WAIVER. On its own EUR 350/month is not enough to live on and pays no tuition. EAMT separately offers scholarships to NON-EU students at BA and MA level covering EITHER 25% OR 50% OF THE TUITION FEE, awarded via scholarship auditions held in September-October - see https://eamt.ee/en/studies/study-grants-and-scholarships/ and https://eamt.ee/en/studies/tuition-fees/ . The two together (50% tuition waiver plus EUR 350/month) is the only combination at EAMT that approaches viability, and both hinge on the same September-October audition/application period, so that month is the pinch point for the Estonian route.

name: Deutschlandstipendium (and the German public-institution fee position)

subjectScope: ALL SUBJECTS - so a production/sound master's at HfMT Koln or FH Dortmund is in scope, subject to the institution running the scheme.

notes: THE GERMAN FUNDING PICTURE FOR HIM, STATED PLAINLY. At HfMT Koln and FH Dortmund - both in North Rhine-Westphalia - there are NO general tuition fees; students pay only a semester contribution (typically a few hundred euros, which includes a public transport pass). So the German problem is NOT tuition, it is LIVING COSTS plus the blocked-funding proof required for the student visa. Deutschlandstipendium at EUR 300/month covers only a fraction of that. Institution-specific scholarship provision at HfMT Koln and FH Dortmund is UNVERIFIED - no dedicated international master's scholarship page was located for either. The binding constraint in Germany is LANGUAGE, not money: without C1 German he cannot access the German-taught production masters at all, and Baden-Wuerttemberg (Popakademie) additionally charges non-EU fees.

name: French public-university fee position for non-EU students - droits differencies and exonerations
provider: Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur et de la Recherche; applied by each institution (UBO Brest, Universite Gustave Eiffel, ESAV Toulouse via Universite Toulouse Jean Jaures)
whoCanApply: All extra-community students (outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland) are, save exceptions, liable for the differentiated registration fees. Institutions may exonerate a capped share of them.

numberOfAwards: QUOTA - AND IT IS SHRINKING. Decret n. 2026-385 of 19 May 2026 sets the exoneration ceiling at 30% of extra-community students in 2026-2027, 25% IN 2027-2028, and 20% from 2028. His entry year, 2027-2028, falls under the 25% cap. Students already exonerated in 2025-2026 keep the old regime for the …

notes: WHY THIS IS RECORDED AS A FUNDING ITEM: for a francophone Tunisian, a French public master's at EUR 255 after exoneration is cheaper than any scholarship elsewhere would make a fee-paying programme. The exoneration IS the funding. THE NEW RISK IS THE TIGHTENING QUOTA - by his 2027-2028 entry year the ceiling drops to 25%, so exoneration can no longer be assumed and he should ask each target institution (UBO Brest, Universite Gustave Eiffel, ESAV Toulouse) in writing about its exoneration policy BEFORE choosing. Note also that the standard French student-aid route, the CROUS bourse sur criteres sociaux, is not generally open to a newly-arrived foreign student, and Eiffel is subject-barred for the arts (see the separate Eiffel record). Institution-specific scholarships at UBO Brest, ESAV Toulouse and Universite Gustave Eiffel are UNVERIFIED - no dedicated international master's scholarship page was located for any of the three.
